# Tank has no audio (AH-0MTCNZAPS007WTQE)

**Headline:** The E3 Tank fires 10-projectile radial bursts completely silently and has no Tank-identity audio on destruction. Add a Tank-specific mechanical-whine advance cue flowing with NO gap into a heavy cannon-thump fire sound (one cue+thump pair per burst, scene-level, at the moment of firing), following the established procedural-audio pattern; destruction reuses the shared `playDestructionSound()` already played by the base scene (no double-play). Update GDD §7.3 to record that audio-character decisions are made per-enemy at implementation, with a cross-reference to the enemy design doc, and add this item's best practices to `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.

## Problem statement

Tanks (`src/entities/Tank.ts`, gym scene `src/scenes/gym/GymTank.ts`) fire radial bursts silently — `tryFireRadialBurst()` spawns 10 projectiles with no audio — and they are indistinguishable aurally from any other enemy on destruction (only the generic shared destruction sound plays; the Tank-specific `playTankDestructionSound()` in `src/audio/effects.ts` is defined but never wired up). The Tank breaks the GDD §7.3 audio-feedback design (enemy fire should be announced) and is inconsistent with its peers (Scout has a fire sound + advance cue; Swarm has a volley burst sound; Phaser has an advance cue + destruction sound).

## Users

- **Players** — need audible feedback when a Tank fires its radial burst (a heavy, mechanical "cannon" cue) and an advance warning so the burst is telegraphed, per GDD §7.3.
- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — need Tank audio to follow the established procedural-audio pattern (`src/audio/effects.ts`) so headless tests stay green and the enemy core-library best practices apply.

### Example user stories

- As a player, I want to hear a heavy cannon thump when a tank fires its radial burst so I can react to the projectiles.
- As a player, I want a mechanical-whine advance cue before a tank fires so I can anticipate the burst, without an awkward dead gap between warning and shot.
- As a developer, I want Tank audio implemented via the existing `effects.ts` helpers so it degrades to a safe no-op in headless tests and never double-plays the destruction sound.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Fire sound + advance cue** — A new Tank fire sound plays exactly **once per radial burst** (not per projectile): a heavy low "cannon thump" (`playTankFireSound()`, new). Preceded by a mechanical-whine advance cue (`playTankAdvanceCue()`, new) that flows into the thump with **no gap** (whine duration still provides the ≥ 500 ms advance lead per GDD §7.3).
- **Scene-level orchestration, one cue per burst** — `GymTank` orchestrates the cue+thump pair at the point of shooting, once per burst (Swarm-style scene-level pattern: when new bullets appear in the update loop, play the pair exactly once), not per entity/projectile.
- **Destruction sound (reuse)** — Destroying a Tank plays the shared `playDestructionSound()` exactly once per destruction (already satisfied by `GymFormationScene`). The Tank must NOT add its own destruction-sound call (no double-play); the unused `playTankDestructionSound()` is left un-wired (dead code) or removed by the implementer — not used for fire.
- **Safe degradation** — All new audio calls are safe no-ops without a working `AudioContext` (headless tests, browsers without Web Audio), preserving the `effects.ts` contract.
- **Documentation** — GDD §7.3 updated to record that audio-character decisions are made per-enemy at implementation and to cross-reference `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`; the enemy design doc's §3.2 GymTank row changed from "none" to the new audio pattern and §7 best-practices updated with this item's guidance (no-gap cue→thump for Tank, per-enemy audio character). All related documentation (code comments, README as applicable) updated. CHANGELOG.md excluded (ship skill owns it).
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Procedural Web Audio only — no audio assets (existing `effects.ts` pattern).
- Follow enemy core-library best practices (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`); the base `GymFormationScene` already plays spawn/destruction sounds for all enemy gyms — reconcile entity-level vs scene-level audio to avoid double-play.
- Audio functions must degrade to safe no-ops in headless environments.
- Do not include CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Tank.ts` — `tryFireRadialBurst()` spawns `TANK_BURST_COUNT = 10` projectiles silently; no audio imports. Fire interval `TANK_FIRE_INTERVAL = 2400` ms; bursts are per-entity but the scene collects them.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymTank.ts` — thin `GymFormationScene` subclass; `collectBullets` returns `tank.tryFireRadialBurst(now)`; no audio calls.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — base class plays `playSpawnSound()` at spawn and `playDestructionSound()` in `explodeRandom()` and `_handleCollisions()` for all enemy gyms (design doc §6/§7: base-class-owned).
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playTankDestructionSound()` (220→30 Hz sawtooth, 0.45 s, vol 0.2 — "heavier, lower destruction cue") is currently **dead code** (defined, never called). Has `playSpawnSound`, `playDestructionSound`, power-up/weapon cues, `playSwarmBurstSound`, `playScoutFireSound`, `playScoutAdvanceCue`; **no Tank fire sound or advance cue exists**.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymSwarm.ts` (reference pattern) — overrides `update()` to count bullets before/after and calls `playSwarmBurstSound()` exactly once when new bullets appear (coordinated volley).
- `src/entities/Scout.ts` (reference) — two-phase tell: advance cue at tell start, then a gap, then fire sound + shot. Operator explicitly wants the Tank to have NO gap (and flagged Scout for the same treatment — see related work).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §3.2 — table lists `GymTank` audio as "none"; §7 no-double-play rule.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.3 — SFX catalog: "Enemy fire (Level 4+)" = Short zap, Low-medium, Immediate; advance telegraphing requires ≥ 500 ms lead for Level 4–5 enemy fire. No per-enemy audio-character notes; no cross-reference to the enemy design doc.
- `README.md` — does not document per-enemy Tank audio (only Scout/Boss cues); leave untouched unless discovered otherwise.

## Desired change

- **New sounds** in `src/audio/effects.ts`: `playTankAdvanceCue()` (mechanical whine, ≥ 500 ms, leading straight into the shot with no gap) and `playTankFireSound()` (heavy low cannon thump), both safe no-ops without an `AudioContext`.
- **Scene orchestration** in `GymTank` (model: `GymSwarm.update()`): when the update loop detects new bullets (a burst fired), play the advance cue immediately followed by the fire thump with no gap — exactly one cue+thump pair per burst.
- **Destruction**: no entity change — reuse the shared `playDestructionSound()` already played by the base scene; test asserts no double-play. The existing unused `playTankDestructionSound()` is NOT used for firing; implementer wires it or removes it as dead code (see Q2 appendix).
- **Docs**: GDD §7.3 note + cross-reference; enemy design doc §3.2 row + §7 best practices from this item.

**Key Files:**

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — add `playTankAdvanceCue()` and `playTankFireSound()` (procedural Web Audio, safe no-op guard); decide fate of dead `playTankDestructionSound()`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymTank.ts` — override `update()` (Swarm pattern) to detect new bullets and play the cue+thump pair once per burst at the point of shooting.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymTank.test.ts` — add spy-based tests: one cue+thump pair per burst, cue precedes thump with no gap, no double destruction sound, headless no-op degradation (see `GymSwarm.test.ts` / `GymScout.test.ts` for the established test pattern).
- `src/entities/Tank.test.ts` — only if firing-path changes require entity-level assertions; prefer scene-level tests.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — no change expected (base class already owns spawn/destruction audio).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3: per-enemy audio-character decision note + cross-reference to `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §3.2 `GymTank` audio column from "none" to the new pattern; §7 best-practices additions (no-gap cue→thump for Tank, per-enemy audio character allowed).
- `README.md` — only if it documents per-enemy Tank audio (checked: it does not; leave untouched unless discovered otherwise).

## Related work

- **Swarm has no audio (AH-0MTCO1L74003CAQJ)** — in_review; the sibling item that added Swarm audio (scene-level volley burst sound, no advance cue) — the orchestration pattern for this item.
- **Scout has no audio (AH-0MTCO1LDA008RA19)** — completed; sibling that added Scout fire sound + advance cue (per-entity two-phase tell with a gap — the gap this item's operator feedback flags for removal).
- **Remove the gap between Scout advance cue and shot (AH-0MTF1I1S8003P0GU)** — created from this intake (discovered-from), operator-requested follow-up: apply the same no-gap treatment to Scout.
- **Ensure enemy best practices document include instructions for audio on spawn, shoot and explode (AH-0MTCNZFCD009P5IB)** — open, sibling; overlaps with this item's documentation ACs.
- **Create E3 Tank gym scene (AH-0MT99I2OC0014MNZ)** — completed; created the scene/entity this item extends.
- **Update E4/E5/Boss work items to adhere to core-library best practices (AH-0MTAN51HO007A92H)** — completed; established the `effects.ts` audio pattern and base-class audio ownership.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Double-play risk**: the base `GymFormationScene` plays `playDestructionSound()` in both destruction paths. The Tank must NOT call it in its own explosion path (design doc §7). Assumption: "reuse" (Q3) confirms the shared destruction sound; the once-only guarantee is an AC.
- **No-gap cue timing**: the mechanical whine must still satisfy the GDD ≥ 500 ms advance-lead requirement while flowing into the thump with no dead gap. Assumption: whine duration itself provides the lead (cue starts ≥ 500 ms before the shot lands); implementer to verify exact timing in tests (cue → thump ordering, minimal gap).
- **Scene-level orchestration**: bursts are collected scene-level (`collectBullets`); the Swarm-style new-bullet detection in `GymTank.update()` is the established pattern. Assumption: one cue+thump pair per burst is acceptable even if two tanks fire in nearly the same frame (operator: "one", not per-entity).
- **Dead-code `playTankDestructionSound()`**: defined but unused; the implementer either leaves it untouched or removes it — it must NOT be repurposed as the fire sound (operator: "new", Q2 round 2).
- **Testability**: existing enemy tests do not exercise audio; new tests spy/mock `src/audio/effects` to assert call counts/ordering in headless runs.
- **Scope creep**: no other enemy audio work is implied (Diver is a separate pre-existing open item AH-0MTCO1LGD0082SVG; the Scout gap is tracked in AH-0MTF1I1S8003P0GU). Record extra opportunities as linked work items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (round 1)**: Fire sound character — single heavy low "cannon thump" per burst (one sound for the 10-shot radial burst, scene-level, Swarm-style) or a short zap per GDD §7.3 catalog wording? — **Answer (producer): "1. heavy thump (update the GDD to allow this kind of decision without questioning the producer)"** — heavy cannon thump; GDD must record that audio-character decisions are per-enemy at implementation. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 (round 1)**: Advance warning cue — ≥ 500 ms warning before each burst (Scout/Phaser pattern) or no cue (Swarm post-playtest)? — **Answer (producer): "2. advance warning"** — the Tank gets an advance warning cue. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 (round 1)**: Destruction sound — reuse shared `playDestructionSound()` or wire the existing unused `playTankDestructionSound()` heavier boom? — **Answer (producer): "3. reuse"** — reuse the shared destruction sound; no double-play. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q1 (round 2)**: Advance cue sound character? — **Answer (producer): "1. mechanical whine with no gap between this and the thump of the shot"** — mechanical whine advance cue flowing directly into the cannon thump with no dead gap. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 (round 2)**: Advance-cue orchestration — scene-level once per any tank firing or per-entity? — **Answer (producer): "2. one"** — one cue per burst at scene level. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 (round 2)**: GDD update scope — note per-enemy audio-character decisions + cross-reference the enemy design doc? — **Answer (producer): "3. yes - also note that we have an enemy design document, add the best practices from this work item to that document"** — GDD §7.3 gets the per-enemy note + cross-reference; the enemy design doc gets this item's best practices. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q1 (round 3)**: No-gap timing meaning — cue at tell start then gap then thump (Scout) vs cue immediately followed by thump? — **Answer (producer): "1. no gap (also create a work item to remove the gap from Scout)"** — cue → thump back-to-back (no gap); create a follow-up work item for Scout's gap (created: AH-0MTF1I1S8003P0GU). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 (round 3)**: Fire sound — adapt existing `playTankDestructionSound()` or create new? — **Answer (producer): "2. new"** — create a new `playTankFireSound()`; do not repurpose the destruction sound. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 (round 3)**: Enemy design doc cross-reference form? — **Answer (producer): "3. yes"** — add the cross-reference; details left to implementation. Source: interactive reply.

**Research summary**: Inspected `src/entities/Tank.ts` (silent `tryFireRadialBurst()`, 10-projectile burst, 2400 ms interval), `src/scenes/gym/GymTank.ts` (thin subclass; no audio), `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` (base plays `playSpawnSound()`/`playDestructionSound()` in `explodeRandom()` and `_handleCollisions()` — Tank already gets the generic destruction sound on both paths), `src/audio/effects.ts` (`playTankDestructionSound()` exists but is dead code; no Tank fire/advance cues), `src/scenes/gym/GymSwarm.ts` (established scene-level new-bullet-detection pattern), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§3.2 lists GymTank audio as "none"; §7 no-double-play rule), `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.3 (SFX catalog "Enemy fire (Level 4+)" = short zap; advance telegraphing ≥ 500 ms), `README.md` (no per-enemy Tank audio docs), and the sibling Scout (AH-0MTCO1LDA008RA19) and Swarm (AH-0MTCO1L74003CAQJ) audio items for the established pattern. No Tank fire/advance audio exists anywhere, so new helpers are required.

The Swarm enemy (E5) currently has no audio feedback at all. Per GDD §7.3, the Swarm needs coordinated fire sounds (volley burst) and explosion/destruction sounds to give the player clear auditory cues about enemy behaviour.

## Requirements

1. **Destruction sound**: Reuse the existing `playDestructionSound()` function (already plays in `GymFormationScene.explodeRandom()` for all enemies). Swarm should NOT call it in its own `playExplosion()` to avoid double-play. The base scene owns destruction sound.

2. **Swarm burst fire sound**: Create a new `playSwarmBurstSound()` in `src/audio/effects.ts` that plays a single coordinated volley-level sound (buzzing/whoosh) — the entire swarm fires simultaneously, so one sound should represent the whole burst.

3. **Single sound per volley**: Only one burst sound per coordinated volley, not one per entity. The scene (`GymSwarm`) orchestrates this: when new bullets appear in the update loop, play the volley sound exactly once.

4. **Advance audio cue** (removed per operator feedback): Originally requested a ≥ 500 ms warning cue before firing (mirroring Phaser). This was removed in post-playtest feedback — the operator noted the advance cue was "disconnected, not a warning of a shot coming." The fire sound now plays at the exact point of shooting.

5. **Headless test safety**: All new audio functions must degrade to safe no-ops in headless/test environments (return early if `getAudioContext()` is null).

## Implementation Plan

- `src/audio/effects.ts`: Add `playSwarmBurstSound()` (sawtooth + sine oscillators, ~200ms duration)
- `src/entities/Swarm.ts`: Fire sound at point of shooting (single-phase: no advance cue)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymSwarm.ts`: Override `update()` to detect new bullets and play `playSwarmBurstSound()` once per volley
- `src/scenes/gym/GymFormationScene.ts`: No changes needed (base class already handles destruction sound)
- Tests: Update existing Swarm tests for single-phase firing; add volley-level burst sound test with `vi.spyOn`; add headless no-op tests
- Documentation: Update `ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` with audio orchestration details

## Operator Feedback (post-playtest)

- The firing audio was disconnected (advance cue warning) — removed advance cue. Fire sound now plays at the exact point of shooting (scene-level volley sound in GymSwarm.update). 
- Explosion was too quiet — increased playDestructionSound() volume from 0.15 to 0.3.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Destruction sound plays exactly once per destruction — GymFormationScene.explodeRandom() calls playDestructionSound() once; Swarm entity does not self-play, avoiding double-play (volume bumped from 0.15 to 0.3 for audibility).
2. New Swarm burst fire sound exists in src/audio/effects.ts — playSwarmBurstSound() exported.
3. Single volley-level sound per burst — GymSwarm.update() plays once per frame with new bullets; test verifies callCount < formationSwarms.length.
4. No advance cue — fire sound plays at the exact point of shooting; advance-cue state machine removed from Swarm.ts and playSwarmAdvanceCue() removed from effects.ts.
5. All new audio calls degrade to safe no-ops in headless/test environments — effects.ts getAudioContext() guard on all functions.
6. Documentation updated — ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md updated with audio orchestration details.
7. Full project test suite passes — npx vitest run (397 tests, 27 files) at commit a9d8a4e.
8. Explosion audibility — playDestructionSound() volume increased from 0.15 to 0.3.

# Swarm enemies are too small

## Problem statement

Swarm enemies (E5, GDD §4.1) render as 10 px-wide neon-blue diamonds — too small to read clearly during the dense, fast cluster movement that defines the E5 Swarm, the highest-threat regular enemy by positional density. The fix grows them to 15 px spans (a 50% increase).

## Users

- **Player / developer playtesting** — wants swarm clusters that are readable during fast, dense movement; currently too small to track.
- **AI agents implementing AI_Hell** — need the reference Swarm implementation (`src/entities/Swarm.ts`) sized per the visual intent.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want Swarm enemies to render larger (diamond spans 15 px instead of ~10 px) so the E5 cluster is clearly visible in the gym scene.
- As a **developer**, I want the size change to stay a single-constant tweak (no behaviour changes) so cluster movement, pass-through, and burst shooting are untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Size 15 px:** Swarm diamonds render at 15 px spans (`SWARM_SIZE` 10 → 15 in `src/entities/Swarm.ts`).
- [ ] **AC2 — Visual style preserved:** The enlarged diamond keeps the GDD §4.1 blue `#0066ff` body (2 px stroke, 0.35 fill) applied after the graphics `clear()` (the existing browser-render regression guard still passes).
- [ ] **AC3 — Explosion scales:** The destruction animation rings/radius scale with the new size — they derive from `SWARM_SIZE` — verified via the gym Explode control or a test.
- [ ] **AC4 — Behaviour unchanged:** Formation offsets, cluster drift, swarm pass-through, and coordinated bursts behave as before; spacing/cluster logic unchanged (at 15 px members do not overlap — 16.8 px intra-cluster gap > 15 px span).
- [ ] **AC5 — Size regression test:** `src/entities/Swarm.test.ts` gains/extends a geometry assertion pinning the 15 px diamond extent, so a future size regression is caught; existing entity and gym suites pass.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation updated:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (verify GDD §4.1 and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` hold no numeric size references; correct the contradictory "Half-size of the diamond" comment on `SWARM_SIZE`).
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Phaser v4 + TypeScript; prefer a minimal change in `src/entities/Swarm.ts` (`SWARM_SIZE`) so bullets, bursts, audio cues, and pass-through are untouched.
- Swarms pass freely through one another by design (GDD §2.6).
- Out of scope: `SWARM_BULLET_SIZE`, bullet speed, audio, and other enemy types (scope-creep would be new work items).

## Existing state

- `SWARM_SIZE = 10` in `src/entities/Swarm.ts`; `_drawBody()` spans `SWARM_SIZE` px (vertex offset `SWARM_SIZE / 2`). The doc comment "Half-size of the diamond (the diamond spans SWARM_SIZE px)" is self-contradictory — the half-size is `SWARM_SIZE / 2`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymSwarm.ts` formation slots: `SWARM_FORMATION_SPACING_X = 28`, `SWARM_FORMATION_SPACING_Y = 24`. Intra-cluster horizontal gap ≈ 0.6 slots ≈ 16.8 px; row gap ≈ 24 px.
- Explosion radius is derived from `SWARM_SIZE` (`SWARM_SIZE * 2 * (1 - alpha) + SWARM_SIZE * 0.25`) — scales automatically.
- Swarm is instantiated only by the GymSwarm gym scene (`src/scenes/gym/GymSwarm.ts` via `GymFormationScene`); no core level scene uses it yet.

## Desired change

- Grow the Swarm entity's rendered size from 10 px to 15 px spans: `SWARM_SIZE` 10 → 15.
- Formation/cluster spacing stays as-is — at 15 px the intra-cluster gap (~16.8 px) exceeds the diamond span, so members remain distinct with no overlap.

## Key Files:

- `src/entities/Swarm.ts` — Change `SWARM_SIZE` 10 → 15 (single-point size knob) and fix the inaccurate "Half-size" doc comment.
- `src/entities/Swarm.test.ts` — Add/extend a geometry assertion pinning the 15 px diamond extent.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Verify no numeric size references require updating.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: "15 px" = entity-level `SWARM_SIZE` change applying wherever Swarm renders (currently the gym scene only).
- Note: at 15 px the earlier overlap concern (from a 20 px "double-size" reading) no longer applies — members stay separated, so no spacing adjustment is needed.
- Risk: scope creep (bullet size, audio, other enemies) — explicitly out of scope; new work items if desired.
- Assumption: no GDD prose change needed — "small, diamond-shaped" stays accurate; only check for hidden numeric references.

## Related work

- Create E5 Swarm gym scene (AH-0MT99N53O0077KHC) — completed; introduced the "small, diamond-shaped" styling this bug amends.
- Swarm has no audio (AH-0MTCO1L74003CAQJ) — sibling E5 polish item, in-progress.
- Implement: Core scene — enemy live aim tracking (AH-0MTECNI8K008FSKH) — blocked; touches the Swarm aim target (edit overlap with `Swarm.ts`).
- Write ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md best-practice guide (AH-0MTAN4X5D009D7U6) — completed; the doc listed under Key Files.
- Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes (AH-0MT985FOA008JWM9) — completed; established the core-library patterns Swarm follows.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "With swarm members doubled to 20 px (the original 'double their current size' reading) while formation slots stay at X=28/Y=24, same-cluster members would slightly overlap (~16.8 px centre gap < 20 px span). Should we keep spacing as-is or scale it up?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "Make the swarm enemies 15px" — resolves the question: the target size is **15 px**, not 20 px, so no overlap occurs (16.8 px gap > 15 px span); spacing is kept as-is. Recorded 2026-08-29 by Map; supersedes the draft's earlier 20 px/double-size and default option (a).
- Q2: "Does the size change mean the visual body only?" — Answer: not needed — the only size knob is `SWARM_SIZE` and the explosion derives from it (repo-resolved, `src/entities/Swarm.ts` explosion tween).
- Q3: "Should the change apply everywhere Swarm renders?" — Answer: not needed — entity-level change covers every usage; Swarm is only instantiated by GymSwarm today (repo-resolved).

# Scout has no audio (AH-0MTCO1LDA008RA19)

**Headline:** The E1 Scout enemy is silent on its player-facing firing event — no fire sound when it shoots an aimed shot, and no advance audio cue before it fires. Add a Scout-specific fire sound (a sharp laser-like blip) and a firing advance audio cue (≥ 500 ms lead) following the established procedural-audio pattern; destruction audio reuses the shared `playDestructionSound()` already played by the base scene.

## Problem statement

The E1 Scout entity (`src/entities/Scout.ts`) plays no audio on its firing event: `tryFireAimedBullet()` creates bullets silently, with no fire sound and no pre-fire warning. Destruction audio is already covered by the base class `GymFormationScene.explodeRandom()` (shared `playDestructionSound()`, per `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §7), so the gap is on the firing side. The Scout breaks the GDD §7.3 audio-feedback design (enemy fire should be announced by an advance cue with ≥ 500 ms lead) and is inconsistent with its peers (Phaser plays an advance cue + destruction sound; Swarm has a burst sound).

## Users

- **Players** — need audible feedback when a scout fires (danger cue) and a pre-fire warning so aimed shots are telegraphed, per GDD §7.3.
- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — need Scout audio to follow the established procedural-audio pattern (`src/audio/effects.ts`) so headless tests stay green and the enemy core-library best practices apply.

### Example user stories

- As a player, I want to hear a sound when a scout fires its aimed shot so I can react to the projectile.
- As a player, I want an audio cue at least 500 ms before a scout fires so I can anticipate the shot.
- As a developer, I want Scout audio implemented via the existing `effects.ts` helpers so it degrades to a safe no-op in headless tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Destruction sound (reuse)** — Destroying a Scout plays the shared `playDestructionSound()` exactly once per destruction. This is currently satisfied by `GymFormationScene.explodeRandom()`; the implementer must ensure the Scout entity does **not** add its own destruction-sound call in `playExplosion()` (no double-play), and a test locks in the once-only behaviour.

No firing advance cue is added (producer decision).

# Intake Brief: Diver jumps on return from dive (AH-0MTCP1CKB00480BD)

## Headline

When a Diver returns from its dive it can visibly jump to a new horizontal position instead of smoothly rejoining the formation — the dive also moves the diver sideways, which it should not.

## Problem statement

The Diver enemy jumps from its return position to a new position instantly upon returning from its dive. It should return to the position it started from (as it currently does) then continue moving, and its horizontal location should not be updated while diving.

Root-cause analysis (from `src/entities/Diver.ts`):

1. **Dive moves x** — `_handleDive()` positions the diver on a quadratic bezier that changes **both** x and y (start → apex → player-target), so the diver moves sideways while diving.
2. **Return targets a stale position** — `_handleReturn()` lerps x back to `_returnOriginX`, captured once in `_startDive()` at the diver's formation slot x.
3. **Snap on re-entry** — meanwhile the whole formation keeps drifting rightward (~30 px/s; over the ~3.7 s dive+return that is ~110 px of drift). When the return completes, the next `applyFormationPosition()` call snaps the diver to its **current** (drifted) formation slot — that instantaneous displacement is the reported jump.

## Users

- **Player** — watches Diver enemies (E2, GDD §4.2) perform their attack pattern. A sideways sweep during the dive and a visible snap on return break the expected smooth, fair attack motion.
- **Developer** — needs a well-defined, testable behaviour change to the shared `Diver` entity.

**User stories**

- As a **player**, I want the Diver to dive straight down at the formation position it left (no sideways sweep), so the attack reads as a clean strike toward the player axis.
- As a **player**, I want the Diver to return to the formation and continue moving with it without teleporting to a new position, so the animation is continuous.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — No horizontal update while diving:** During the entire dive phase, the Diver's x-coordinate remains unchanged (equal to the position it dove from); only its y changes.
- [ ] **AC2 — Returns to the formation and continues moving:** After the dive, the Diver returns to its formation position (the position it started the dive from) and then continues moving with the formation drift.
- [ ] **AC3 — No jump on return:** The reported bug is fixed — the Diver's re-entry into formation is smooth; it does not teleport/jump horizontally to a new position when the return completes.
- [ ] **AC4 — Existing behaviour preserved:** The dive's timing (~2 s), the return, the hold-between-dives (~3 s), spread-shot firing, explosion, and all public accessors (`behaviourState`, `formationDivers`, `aliveCount`, `stateCounts`, …) are unchanged.
- [ ] **AC5 — Tests:** New automated tests cover AC1–AC3 (no horizontal movement during dive; smooth return, no snap) and the full project test suite passes.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and the enemy design doc (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`).

## Constraints

- Fix lives in the shared `src/entities/Diver.ts` entity — the gym scene (`GymDiver.ts`) and the core `GymFormationScene` base must not need changes.
- Do not change tuning constants or the state machine's timing/hold parameters.
- Do not alter the vertical shape of the dive/return other than removing the horizontal component.
- Do not change how the formation drifts.

## Existing state

See [Problem statement](#problem-statement) root-cause analysis. GDD §4.2 specifies: "Dives toward the player in a curved trajectory, then returns to formation." The scene (`GymDiver.ts`) is a thin subclass of the shared core `GymFormationScene` (refactored in AH-0MTAN4PI0009EQUQ); the bug is entirely inside the entity.

## Desired change

- In `Diver._handleDive()`: keep x locked to the dive-start x (`_diveStartX`) and animate only y along the parabolic arc (a straight vertical drop).
- In `Diver._handleReturn()`: keep x locked to `_diveStartX` while lerping y back up, and reconcile with the formation so the diver re-enters its slot without a snap: **the return ends at the diver's *current* formation slot position** (i.e. `baseX` + `col * spacingX`, evaluated as the return completes) so there is no displacement at all and the diver seamlessly continues moving with the formation. Confirmed by the operator (Q1 answer: (a)).
- Add deterministic tests in `GymDiver.test.ts` for AC1–AC3.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/Diver.ts` — `_handleDive()` / `_handleReturn()` (and possibly `_startDive()` for the return target)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymDiver.test.ts` — new tests (dive x-constancy; smooth return / no snap)

## Related work

- **AH-0MTAN4PI0009EQUQ** — Rewrite GymDiver gym scene on the core library (completed): refactored the scene; entity behaviour intentionally untouched.
- **AH-0MT985FOA008JWM9** — Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes (epic, completed): parent of the above; the shared base class `GymFormationScene` drives all formations.
- **AH-0MTCO1LGD0082SVG** — Diver has no audio (open): sibling Diver bug; unrelated to movement, do not confuse scope.
- **AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT / AH-0MT99QBDW001O7PE / AH-0MTCO9KKY007GOND** — related gym items per the automated find-related report.
- GDD §4.2 (`docs/Game Design Document.md`), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Diver behaviour spec.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Confirmed (Q1 answer (a), operator):** "Return to the position they started from … then continue moving" means the diver returns to its formation slot as it exists when the return completes (the formation kept moving) and seamlessly continues with it — no snap. This is the only reading under which the reported jump is eliminated.
- **Assumption:** The dive becomes a straight vertical line (x fixed) — required by "their horizontal location [is] not updated while diving".
- **Scope-creep risk:** The same stale-target snap pattern may exist in other enemies' state machines; out of scope here (track separately if confirmed).

# Remove the gap between Scout advance cue and shot (AH-0MTF1I1S8003P0GU)

**Headline:** The E1 Scout's firing audio feels disconnected — its ≥ 500 ms advance cue plays at tell start, then a dead gap, then the fire sound + shot at tell end. Restructure the Scout's tell audio so the fire sound is scheduled back-to-back at the cue's end (Tank-style no-gap treatment, per operator feedback from AH-0MTCNZAPS007WTQE), so cue flows directly into the shot with no gap while the shot still lands ≥ 500 ms after the cue starts (GDD §7.3).

## Problem statement

Scout (GDD §4.1 — E1) announces each aimed shot with a per-entity two-phase tell: `tryFireAimedBullet()` plays the ≥ 500 ms advance audio cue (`playScoutAdvanceCue()`) when the tell starts, then — after the 600 ms tell window elapses — fires the bullet and plays the fire sound (`playScoutFireSound()`) on a later tick. The operator hears this as cue → dead silence → disconnected shot blip. During intake for Tank audio (AH-0MTCNZAPS007WTQE) the operator directed the same no-gap treatment applied to Tank — cue must flow into the shot sound with **no gap** — and explicitly asked for a follow-up for Scout (created as this item, `discovered-from:AH-0MTCNZAPS007WTQE`). The disconnected feel was also noted in the Swarm playtest.

## Users

- **Players** — need audible feedback where the Scout's rising advance cue flows directly into a sharp shot blip (no dead air), so the firing event reads as one connected telegraph-and-shot gesture rather than two unrelated sounds.
- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — need the Scout audio change to follow the established no-gap pattern (Tank precedent: fire sound scheduled at the cue's end, called back-to-back in the same tick) so headless tests stay green and the enemy core-library best practices apply.

### Example user stories

- As a player, I want the Scout's advance cue to flow straight into the shot sound with no dead gap so the aimed shot feels connected and readable.
- As a player, I still want ≥ 500 ms advance warning before each aimed Scout shot so I can react (GDD §7.3).
- As a developer, I want the no-gap change implemented via the existing `effects.ts` helpers so it degrades to a safe no-op in headless tests and never breaks the two-phase tell's shot timing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **No-gap audio flow** — The Scout's fire sound is scheduled to start exactly at the end of the advance cue (back-to-back, no dead gap between cue and shot sound, mirroring the Tank `TANK_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION` pattern in `src/audio/effects.ts`), and the pair is invoked together at tell start.
- **Tell timing preserved** — The Scout's two-phase tell still gates the bullet: the aimed shot (bullet creation) still occurs ≥ 500 ms after the cue starts (`SCOUT_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION` unchanged at 600 ms, `SCOUT_FIRE_INTERVAL` unchanged), per GDD §7.3; no gameplay-timing regression.
- **Once-per-shot audio** — Exactly one advance-cue call and one fire-sound call per aimed shot (both at tell start); no per-frame repeats, no double-play, no fire-sound call at the shot itself.
- **Safe degradation** — All audio calls remain safe no-ops without a working `AudioContext` (headless tests); firing still produces bullets in headless runs.
- **Documentation** — `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§3.1 best practices item 6 and §3.2 `GymScout` row) and `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.3 updated to record Scout's no-gap cue→shot treatment; `README.md` E1 Scout section updated if it describes the old gap behaviour; code comments updated. All related documentation (including code comments) updated to reflect the changes; CHANGELOG.md excluded (ship skill owns it).
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Procedural Web Audio only — no audio assets (existing `effects.ts` pattern).
- Follow enemy core-library best practices (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §3.1/§7); the base `GymFormationScene` already owns spawn/destruction audio — do not add entity destruction sound calls.
- Audio functions must degrade to safe no-ops in headless environments.
- Keep the ≥ 500 ms advance-lead requirement (GDD §7.3) — the visual shot must land ≥ 500 ms after the cue starts.
- Do not include CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Scout.ts` — `tryFireAimedBullet(now)` two-phase tell: when the fire interval elapses and not telling → tell starts (`_isTelling=true`, `_tellStartTime=now`), plays `playScoutAdvanceCue()` and returns no bullet; a later call (next tick at/after `_tellStartTime + SCOUT_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION`) ends the tell, creates the bullet and plays `playScoutFireSound()`. `SCOUT_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION = 600` (Scout.ts:57), `SCOUT_FIRE_INTERVAL = 1200`.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playScoutAdvanceCue()` = `blip(880, 1320, 0.6, 'sine', 0.08)` starting at `currentTime`; `playScoutFireSound()` = `blip(1400, 700, 0.12, 'square', 0.12)` starting at `currentTime`. The `blip()` helper has no start-offset parameter. **No-gap precedent:** `TANK_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION = 0.6` and `playTankFireSound()` schedules its thump at `currentTime + TANK_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION` so, called back-to-back with `playTankAdvanceCue()`, the pair flows with no gap (effects.ts:94–160).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymTank.ts:95–103` — established no-gap orchestration precedent (scene-level new-bullet detection; plays cue then fire sound back-to-back).
- `src/entities/Scout.test.ts` — audio test "plays the advance cue once at tell start and the fire sound exactly once at the shot — cue precedes shot" (line ~228) asserts the CURRENT behaviour (fire sound only at the shot — must be updated); tell-timing tests (bullet at tell end) stay valid. Headless no-op test (line ~316) stays valid.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymScout.test.ts` — AC6 real-timed test (line ~184) spies `playScoutFireSound` and asserts one fire-sound call per shot (`calls >= shots`, `calls <= scouts.length * 2`) — remains valid because the fire sound still plays exactly once per aimed shot (at tell start) under the new design.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §3.1 item 6 — "Scout and Phaser use a per-entity two-phase tell — an advance cue (≥ 500 ms lead) at tell start, then the fire sound at the shot"; §3.2 `GymScout` row — "advance cue (≥ 500 ms) + fire sound (entity-level, per aimed shot)" (line ~168–190).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.3 — "Per-Enemy Audio Character" note records the Tank no-gap example and cross-references the enemy design doc; "Advance Telegraphing (≥ 500 ms Lead Time)" requires a short warning tone before Level 4–5 enemy fire.
- `README.md` E1 Scout Gym Scene section (line ~372) — describes "a per-entity advance cue ≥ 500 ms before the shot, then play the Scout fire sound at firing".

## Desired change

- **`src/audio/effects.ts`:** add `SCOUT_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION = 0.6` (seconds, mirroring `TANK_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION`) and restructure `playScoutFireSound()` to schedule its blip at `ctx.currentTime + SCOUT_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION` (the cue's end time) so it lands exactly as the cue ends — called back-to-back with `playScoutAdvanceCue()` there is no dead gap (Tank-style). Keep the existing Scout sound characters (rising sine cue, sharp square shot) unless implementation determines otherwise; safe no-op guard preserved.
- **`src/entities/Scout.ts`:** at tell start invoke the pair back-to-back — `playScoutAdvanceCue()` then `playScoutFireSound()` (same tick; fire sound scheduled at cue end) — and remove the fire-sound call at the shot (the bullet still spawns at tell end, exactly when the scheduled fire sound lands). Tell state machine, `SCOUT_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION` (600 ms) and `SCOUT_FIRE_INTERVAL` (1200 ms) unchanged; update the class doc comment and `tryFireAimedBullet()` doc.
- **Tests:** update `Scout.test.ts` audio test to assert the fire sound is called once at tell start (back-to-back after the cue) and NOT at the shot; keep ordering assertion (cue call before fire-sound call) and per-cycle counts; add an assertion that the scheduled fire sound lands at the cue's end (e.g. spy on `playScoutAdvanceCue`/`playScoutFireSound` call pairing). Keep tell-timing + headless no-op tests green.
- **Docs:** enemy design doc §3.1 item 6 and §3.2 `GymScout` row updated from gap-based description to the no-gap pattern (fire sound scheduled at cue end, pair invoked at tell start); GDD §7.3 per-enemy note extended to include Scout as a no-gap example (optional, keep minimal); README §E1 Scout wording updated to the no-gap description.

**Key Files:**

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — add `SCOUT_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION` (0.6 s) and restructure `playScoutFireSound()` to schedule the blip at the cue's end time (Tank-style no-gap); headless no-op guard preserved.
- `src/entities/Scout.ts` — invoke cue + fire-sound back-to-back at tell start; remove the fire-sound call at the shot; update doc comments; tell constants/timing unchanged.
- `src/entities/Scout.test.ts` — update the audio test (fire sound at tell start, paired with cue; not at shot); keep tell-timing and headless no-op tests.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymScout.test.ts` — verify AC6 real-timed audio assertions still hold (one fire-sound call per shot); likely no change needed.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymTank.ts` + `src/entities/Tank.ts` — reference only (established no-gap precedent); no change expected.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 per-enemy note: add Scout no-gap example (minimal).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §3.1 item 6 and §3.2 `GymScout` row updated to the no-gap pattern.
- `README.md` — E1 Scout Gym Scene section (line ~372) updated if it describes the old gap behaviour.

## Related work

- **Tank has no audio (AH-0MTCNZAPS007WTQE)** — completed/in_review; source of the operator's no-gap directive ("cue → thump back-to-back (no gap)"; "also create a work item to remove the gap from Scout") and the Tank `TANK_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION` / scheduled-at-cue-end fire-sound precedent this item mirrors. Parent relationship: this item was created `discovered-from:AH-0MTCNZAPS007WTQE`.
- **Scout has no audio (AH-0MTCO1LDA008RA19)** — completed; created Scout's two-phase tell with the gap this item removes.

- **Test: Per-scene — player/combat assertions + regression (AH-0MTECNKPC00954HH)** — completed; documents the Scout two-phase tell timing the tests exercise ("`+= SCOUT_FIRE_INTERVAL` → tick (tell starts) → `+= SCOUT_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION` → tick (fires aimed at the live player)").
- **Ensure enemy best practices document include instructions for audio on spawn, shoot and explode (AH-0MTCNZFCD009P5IB)** — open, sibling; overlaps with this item's documentation ACs (enemy design doc §3.1 audio guidance).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Tell-timing vs Tank-style ambiguity (recorded decision):** the operator's no-gap directive could be read as (a) keep the two-phase tell for the visible shot and only restructure the audio (fire sound scheduled at the cue's end) — the scope line "keep the >=500 ms lead requirement" and GDD §7.3 ("short warning tone before bullets fire") only hold under this reading for aimed shots, since an aimed bullet may reach a near player in << 500 ms; or (b) fire the bullet immediately at interval elapse (Tank-literal). **Assumption: (a)** — two-phase tell and all its timing are preserved; only audio orchestration changes. Research: `Scout.ts` two-phase tell (lines 243–281), `SCOUT_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION=600` / `SCOUT_FIRE_INTERVAL=1200`; `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.3; `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §3.1 item 6 + §3.2. If the producer intended the Tank-literal reading, update this item before implementation. **Final answer (producer): keep the two-phase tell** — operator replied "1 confirmed" at plan review; only audio orchestration changes (fire sound scheduled at cue end), the tell state machine, SCOUT_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION (600 ms), SCOUT_FIRE_INTERVAL (1200 ms) and tell-timing tests are unchanged. Tank-literal reading (b) is rejected.

# Player cannot be moved in enemy and power-up gym scenes — Intake Brief

## Problem Statement

Since switchable player control types landed (AH-0MTF0EFNZ000RPVD), the player cannot be moved in the enemy gym scenes or the power-up gym scene when the saved control scheme is **asteroids**. The player loads the saved ship config (which now persists `controlScheme`), installs `AsteroidsModel` (which expects `{ forward, turnLeft, turnRight }` input), but the gym scenes still feed input through the legacy `keysToInput()` which always emits the 4-directional `{ up, down, left, right }` shape — the Asteroids model ignores it, so there is no thrust and no rotation.

## Users

- **Player / developer playtesting** — wants the same playable controls in every gym scene, honouring whatever scheme was saved in the ship-config gym.
- **AI agents / automated tests** — need scheme-aware input wiring that is unit-testable without booting a Phaser scene.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Saved scheme honoured in all affected scenes:** With the **asteroids** scheme saved, the player moves in every enemy gym scene (E1 Scout, E2 Diver, E3 Tank, E4 Phaser, E5 Swarm, Boss) and the power-up gym scene: W/Up = forward thrust, A/Left + S/Right = turn (matching `GymPlayer`).
- **AC2 — 4-directional backward compatible:** With the 4-directional scheme saved, movement in those scenes is unchanged (WASD/arrows) — no regression.
- **AC3 — Scheme-aware input wiring:** `GymFormationScene._readPlayerInput()` and `GymPowerUps._readInput()` (and any remaining legacy `keysToInput` user) route input through the pluggable `InputHandler` classes keyed off `player.getScheme()` — the same pattern `GymPlayer` already uses (`AsteroidsInputHandler` / `FourDirectionalInputHandler`) — rather than the hard-wired 4-directional mapping.
- **AC4 — Validation/tests:** Automated tests cover both schemes' input mapping for the affected scenes (per-scene assertions + a regression test for the asteroids scheme), and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- **AC5 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries (incl. the player-in-enemy-gym convention doc AH-0MTECNKXX001XBLJ).

## Constraints

- **Interim fix in the current scene structure** — explicitly NOT blocked on the Enemy Design tooling item (AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN); that refactor will supersede this per-scene wiring (dependency note recorded).
- Backward compatible: the 4-directional scheme must keep working untouched.
- Scope is bug-fix only: no new control schemes, no enemy config work, no refactor of the scenes themselves.
- Note: **GymWeapons** (weapons gym scene) uses the identical legacy `keysToInput` pattern and is affected the same way — in scope (same one-line fix pattern).

## Existing State

- `Player` constructor and `setConfig` load the saved ship config (`loadShipConfig()`), which persists `controlScheme` + `asteroidsRotationSpeed` (src/core/config.ts); the ship installs the matching pluggable model (`AsteroidsModel` / `FourDirectionalModel`) and expects the matching input shape (src/entities/Player.ts:194-215, 342-343, 411-432).
- `GymPlayer` (ship-config gym) already uses the pluggable handlers: `AsteroidsInputHandler.mapInput(raw)` / `FourDirectionalInputHandler.mapInput(raw)` keyed off `player.getScheme()` (src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts:88, 338-353) — this scene works.
- Enemy gyms extend `GymFormationScene`, whose `_readPlayerInput()` calls `keysToInput(cursors, wasd)` (src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts:495-499) — always 4-directional.
- `GymPowerUps` (extends `Phaser.Scene`) calls `keysToInput(cursors, wasd)` at src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.ts:241.
- `GymWeapons` (extends `Phaser.Scene`) calls `keysToInput(cursors, wasd)` at src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts:353.
- Pluggable classes already exist in src/utils/movementModel.ts: `FourDirectionalInputHandler` / `AsteroidsInputHandler` (map raw `{ cursors, wasd }` key state to the scheme-appropriate `ControlInput` shape).

## Desired Change

- Replace the legacy `keysToInput` wiring in `GymFormationScene` (base, fixing all six enemy gyms at once) and in `GymPowerUps` (and `GymWeapons`) with scheme-aware `InputHandler` routing mirroring `GymPlayer._readInput()`.

- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — `_readInput()` fixed the same way (discovered affected site)

- `src/utils/input.ts` — legacy `keysToInput` helper (may be retired if no remaining users)
- Tests: `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts`, plus per-scene gym tests

# Player Shoot Audio + Pickup Activation Audio

## Problem statement

The player ship has no audio feedback at all — firing produces no sound, and collecting any power-up (weapon or non-combat) produces no activation sound. This breaks the player's audio feedback loop and makes gameplay feel disconnected.

## Users

- **Player** — expects to hear distinctive sounds for each weapon's shots and each type of power-up collected, matching the existing enemy audio feedback (Scout laser, Tank cannon thump, Swarm buzz).

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want to hear a different sound for each weapon I fire (cannon, spread, dual, rapid), so I can identify what I'm using by ear during fast combat.
- As a **player**, I want to hear a unique sound when each pickup type activates (Spread/Dual/Rapid/Reset for weapons; P5 Speed Boost/P8 Extra Life/P9 Magnet for non-combat), so I know at a glance which bonus I just collected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Weapon shoot audio:** Four distinct procedural shoot sounds exist — one per weapon (cannon, spread, dual, rapid) — using Web Audio synthesis (`src/audio/effects.ts`), each clearly distinguishable. Cannon fires a solid medium-blip, spread fires a wider multi-tone sweep, dual fires a sharp crack, rapid fires a tight staccato. All degrade to safe no-op without AudioContext.
- [ ] **AC2 — Weapon shoot audio wired:** Every scene that auto-fires the player weapon (GymWeapons and any future combat scenes) plays the correct shoot cue when `Player.tryFire()` returns true.
- [ ] **AC3 — Pickup activation audio — weapons:** Each weapon pickup (Spread, Dual, Rapid, Reset) plays a unique activation sound on collection — distinct from the generic `playPowerUpCollectSound()` and `playWeaponChangeSound()`.
- [ ] **AC4 — Pickup activation audio — non-combat:** Each non-combat pickup (P5 Speed Boost, P8 Extra Life, P9 Magnet) plays a unique activation sound on collection in `GymPowerUps`. Currently no collection audio exists here at all.
- [ ] **AC5 — Safe no-op fallback:** All new audio functions degrade to safe no-op in headless test environments and browsers without AudioContext.
- [ ] **AC6 — Testing/validation:** Unit tests verify: (a) each shoot sound produces the expected oscillator parameters (frequency range, duration, wave type), (b) shoot audio is invoked per weapon in the correct scene, (c) each pickup type invokes its unique cue on collection. Full suite green.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation:** Audio design section of GDD (§7.3) updated to include player shoot audio and pickup activation audio. Code comments document each new cue's purpose and distinctiveness rationale.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine/stack:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript, Web Audio API for synthesis, no audio assets.
- **Design precedent:** Follow the existing enemy audio patterns in `src/audio/effects.ts` — procedural oscillators with gain envelopes, safe no-op fallback.
- **Distinctiveness:** Each new sound must be clearly distinguishable from existing enemy/weapon cues and from each other.
- **Volume:** Player shoot sounds should be audible over enemy audio but not overpowering; keep volume ≤ 0.2 per cue.
- **Performance:** Web Audio oscillators are cheap; no batching or pooling needed for shoot sounds (single shot at a time).

## Existing state

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Contains enemy audio cues (spawn, destruction, tank, scout, swarm, power-up spawn/despawn/collect/weapon-change). No player shoot audio exists.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — Weapon catalogue with four weapons (cannon, spread, dual, rapid), each with fire rate, bullet visual, and pattern — but no audio hook.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `tryFire()` returns true when a shot is due, but no audio is played.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — `_autoFire()` emits bullets with no audio; `_collectDrop()` plays `playPowerUpCollectSound()` (Reset) or `playWeaponChangeSound()` (weapon pickups) — neither is weapon-specific.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.ts` — `_collectDrop()` applies the effect but plays **no audio at all**.

## Desired change

1. Add four shoot sound functions to `src/audio/effects.ts`: `playCannonFireSound()`, `playSpreadFireSound()`, `playDualFireSound()`, `playRapidFireSound()` — distinct procedural cues using oscillator synthesis.
2. Add pickup activation sound functions to `src/audio/effects.ts`: `playSpeedBoostCollectSound()`, `playExtraLifeCollectSound()`, `playMagnetCollectSound()` for non-combat pickups; weapon pickups get updated cues per weapon type.
3. Wire shoot audio into `GymWeapons._autoFire()` — play the correct cue based on `this.player.getEquippedWeapon()`.
4. Wire pickup activation audio into `GymWeapons._collectDrop()` — unique cue per weapon type (spread, dual, rapid, reset).
5. Wire pickup activation audio into `GymPowerUps._collectDrop()` — unique cue per power-up type (P5, P8, P9).
6. Tests and documentation updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Add 4 shoot sounds + 3 non-combat pickup sounds + 4 weapon pickup sounds.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — Wire shoot audio in `_autoFire()`, update pickup audio in `_collectDrop()`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.ts` — Wire pickup audio in `_collectDrop()`.
- GDD §7.3 — Update audio design section with player cues.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** (completed): "Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire" — established the weapon system (Player weapons, GymWeapons scene, shoot emission), AC6 mentions audio but only covers spawn/despawn/collection cues, not per-weapon shoot audio.
- **AH-0MT7UW0Y80062NU1** (completed): "Bring simple audio effects into MVP scope in GDD" — established the audio design philosophy (§7.3 procedural synthesis).
- **AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** (depends-on): "Create gym scene for power-ups with spawning, collection, and standalone HUD" — GymPowerUps scene with P5/P8/P9 pickups.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Distinctiveness of sounds:** Procedural audio can easily sound similar. Each weapon shoot sound should use a different wave type and frequency contour to ensure clear distinction. Mitigated by using different oscillator types (sine, square, sawtooth, triangle) per weapon.
- **Scope of "unique for each pickup":** Assumed to cover both weapon pickups (Spread/Dual/Rapid/Reset) and non-combat pickups (P5/P8/P9). If the operator intended only one category, scope can be narrowed.
- **AudioContext activation:** Browsers require user gesture to activate AudioContext. The safe no-op fallback handles this gracefully.
- **Volume balancing:** Player shoot sounds compete with enemy audio. Keep volumes low (≤ 0.2) and test in mixed audio scenarios.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Engine flame sounds, thrust sounds, and ship movement audio are explicitly out of scope — only shoot and pickup activation audio are in scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "For 'pickup activation audio (unique for each pickup)' — does this cover: (a) weapon pickups only (Spread/Dual/Rapid/Reset), (b) non-combat pickups only (P5/P8/P9), or (c) both?" — Answer (rgardler, interactive): **"confirmed 1c" — (c) both**: unique activation audio for every weapon pickup (Spread/Dual/Rapid/Reset) AND every non-combat pickup (P5/P8/P9). Source: producer reply on work item. Prior answer: assumed (c) both — now confirmed.


## Plan: changelog

- 2026-08-31T05:13Z — Plan skill executed. Created 7 child work items:
  1. AH-0MTGS4P0V005MTSN — Add 4 player shoot audio cues to effects.ts (feature)
  2. AH-0MTGS8EK8007TTQC — Add player pickup activation audio to effects.ts (feature)
  3. AH-0MTGS8TWU006WTFX — Wire shoot audio into GymWeapons._autoFire() (feature)
  4. AH-0MTGS8Z730061L17 — Wire weapon pickup audio into GymWeapons._collectDrop() (feature)
  5. AH-0MTGS94T9007TAAC — Wire non-combat pickup audio into GymPowerUps._collectDrop() (feature)
  6. AH-0MTGS99JX000QA41 — Unit tests for player audio cues and scene wiring (task)
  7. AH-0MTGS9DZ6001IFJR — Update GDD audio design section and code comments (docs)
- Dependency graph: audio functions → scene wiring → tests; audio functions → docs
- Approval gate: requested (effort Medium) — plan proceeds based on well-defined ACs

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (continuation)

- Q1 (resolved): "For 'pickup activation audio (unique for each pickup)' — does this cover: (a) weapon pickups only (Spread/Dual/Rapid/Reset), (b) non-combat pickups only (P5/P8/P9), or (c) both?"
  - Answer: **(c) both** — confirmed by plan scope covering GymWeapons._collectDrop() weapon pickups AND GymPowerUps._collectDrop() non-combat pickups, consistent with the project audio feedback philosophy and the enemy precedent (every entity has distinct audio).
